abstract: Mass photometry (MP) measures the mass of single unlabelled molecules as they adsorb to a glass surface, but conventional analysis captures each molecule only momentarily, as it binds, and neglects its subsequent fate. Here we correct for coverslip drift and use mass-dependent localisation precision to link successive events at one site to a single molecule and enables two workflows for studying protein assemblies. In tandem MP, matching each binding event with its outcomes yields a two-dimensional precursor-product spectrum that separates dissociation from unbinding, providing structural insights into the protein assemblies and the kinetics of subunit loss. By comparing citrate synthase homologues, we reveal distinct fingerprints and disassembly pathways among complexes of the same oligomeric state. In particle tracking, differential imaging allows for continuous recording of particle mass and position. By examining adeno-associated virus capsids, we recovered accurate masses, and reveals acid-induced disassembly and movement behaviour that depends on both viral and imaging surfaces. Our code is freely available and applies to data obtained on commercial instruments with minimal changes to experimental protocols, offering additional dimensions to MP analysis beyond the mass histogram to return time-resolved, single-molecule histories.
